findings.title: Request metrics label uses the raw URL path, so Prometheus cardinality grows with every resource ID
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: request-id.ts labels both HTTP metrics with routeLabel(req) — the matched Express route template (req.route.path + req.baseUrl) with a single 'unmatched' bucket for 404s — instead of req.path; commit d9911286 (OBS-P2-010/PERF-P2-001).

findings.title: Public storefront pages are force-dynamic and uncached; each page view costs two Supabase reads
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the store pages remain force-dynamic but the cost per view is fixed at both layers — apps/web/lib/catalog/catalog-source.ts:47-80 keeps a 60s per-process snapshot (DB-backed snapshots only, tests can invalidate) and the API response-caches the public catalog routes for 60s (routes/store/catalog.ts:21-30,83-123) with a Redis-backed cache and in-memory fallback (middleware/cache.ts); commit f0df4268.

findings.title: resolveEffectivePermissions is uncached and fans out 4-6 queries per gated request
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts:21-124 wraps resolution in a short-TTL cache keyed by userId:orgId that also dedupes concurrent resolutions (in-flight promise is cached) and never caches failures; commit f0df4268.

findings.title: Bulk invite performs 4 sequential Supabase calls per invite and cannot finish 500 invites inside the 30s request timeout
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the DB fan-out is fixed — profiles and memberships are looked up once per 100-entry chunk and memberships are inserted as one multi-row insert per chunk (bulk.ts:22,133-226; duplicates collapsed up front); commit a37b8a4d. Still partially fixed: auth accounts are still invited one at a time inside a sequential loop (bulk.ts:163-190, documented ADMIN-P2-004 rationale), so a worst-case request of 500 brand-new emails remains up to 500 sequential auth-admin calls inside the 30s request deadline (app.ts requestTimeout) — no throughput measurement exists and the per-row results would be lost if the deadline fires.

findings.title: Each SSE notification stream opens its own Supabase Realtime channel with no connection cap
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: notifications.ts:29-41 tracks active streams per process and refuses new ones past SSE_MAX_STREAMS=200 with 503 + Retry-After (:198), releasing the slot on close; commit f0df4268.

findings.title: POST /billing/sync does not paginate Stripe results
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: billing.ts:75-142 fetches every Stripe page with starting_after until has_more is false, bounded by a page cap that reports truncation; commits c735bcb4/ec01772e (BILL-P2-002, ARCH-P2-005).

findings.title: Unbounded list reads remain on compliance and time-entry endpoints; exports load up to 10k rows with select("*")
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the remaining 10,000-row audit export was lowered to the shared EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT (5,000) — routes/audit.ts:95,191; lib/pagination.ts:27 — matching the other exports (approvals/assets/domain-monitors/findings/projects/proposals/tickets and the three services). compliance.ts:34,92 stays at LIST_HARD_CAP=1,000 and final/time-entries.ts caps the summary at 5,000 rows with truncated reporting. Reads are now bounded, with 5,000-row in-memory exports retained by design.

findings.title: Every paginated list request also runs an exact row count
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: pagination.ts:59-69 adds listCountMode(), which defaults to PostgREST `estimated` and only uses `exact` when the caller passes ?withTotal=1; the cited tickets.ts:109 and projects.ts:104 now use it, and the 38 remaining `count: "exact"` call sites are aggregate/search/dashboard endpoints that genuinely need exact totals.

findings.title: No bundle-size or performance budget gate; the analyzer is opt-in only
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: scripts/bundle-budget.json commits total/totalGzip/largest-chunk budgets (measured 2026-10-12 from the deployed image) and scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs runs as a gate in e2e.yml:164, so a bundle regression fails CI; commit 57dc3cc7.

findings.title: API routes broadly select all columns (`select("*")`) and pagination is ad hoc
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: shared-pagination adoption grew from 4 to 43 route files (grep lib/pagination) and listCountMode bounds the count work, but the projection half is untouched — 156 `select("*")` calls remain in non-test API code (was 154) and 37 route files still parse page/limit inline, so list responses keep shipping every column of every row.

findings.title: SLA metrics endpoint reads every SLA row in a 90-day window with `select('*')` and no limit
findings.note: newly identified at 6b7aa1a5 (the route existed at 7dd0402, but the limit gap was not recorded then): apps/api/src/routes/sla.ts:24-30 builds `select('*', { count: 'exact' }).gte('created_at', since)` with `days` up to 90 and never applies a limit or range; :32-56 then loads all rows and computes the summary in memory, returning only the last 20. A busy org can make one dashboard refresh read tens of thousands of full rows (all columns). The response cache is 60s (responseCacheNoRenew), so it bounds repeat cost but not the first read. Fix: aggregate in SQL (count/sum/avg grouped by metric) or page with a LIST_HARD_CAP and a truncated flag; select only the columns the summary needs.

report: 8 verified-fixed, 2 partially-fixed, 0 regressed, 1 open (PERF-P3-005 new); PERF-P3-001 is now fixed by the 5,000-row export cap.
